arxiv-2004-07451.title: Observing the “quantum Cheshire cat” effect with noninvasive weak measurement
arxiv-2004-07451.creator: Yosep Kim, Dong-Gil Im, Yong-Su Kim, Sang-Wook Han, Sung Moon, Yoon-Ho Kim, Young-Wook Cho
arxiv-2004-07451.description: Abstract One of the common conceptions of nature, typically derived from the experiences with classical systems, is that attributes of the matter coexist with the substance. In the quantum regime, however, the quantum particle itself and its physical property may be in spatial separation, known as the quantum Cheshire cat effect.

arxiv-2203-08828.title: Robust quantum many-body scars in lattice gauge theories
arxiv-2203-08828.creator: Jad C. Halimeh, Luca Barbiero, Philipp Hauke, Fabian Grusdt, Annabelle Bohrdt
arxiv-2203-08828.description: Abstract Quantum many-body scarring is a paradigm of weak ergodicity breaking arising due to the presence of special nonthermal many-body eigenstates that possess low entanglement entropy, are equally spaced in energy, and concentrate in certain parts of the Hilbert space.

arxiv-2210-15242.title: Compressed-Sensing-Based 3D Localization with Distributed Passive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
arxiv-2210-15242.creator: Jiguang He, Aymen Fakhreddine, Henk Wymeersch, George C. Alexandropoulos
arxiv-2210-15242.description: Abstract In this paper, the programmable signal propagation paradigm, enabled by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs), is exploited for high accuracy 3 3 -Dimensional (3D) user localization with a single multi-antenna base station. Capitalizing on the tunable reflection capability of passive RISs, we present a two-stage user localization method leveraging the multi-reflection wireless environment.

arxiv-2212-13822.title: Hypergraphs with Polynomial Representation: Introducing r r -splits Thanks: This work was supported by the Agence Nationale de la Recherche under grant ANR-20-CE23-0002
arxiv-2212-13822.creator: François Pitois, Mohammed Haddad, Hamida Seba, Olivier Togni
arxiv-2212-13822.description: Abstract Inspired by the split decomposition of graphs and rank-width, we introduce the notion of r r -splits. We focus on the family of r r -splits of a graph of order n n , and we prove that it forms a hypergraph with several properties.

arxiv-2304-11363.title: Lexicographic Ranking Supermartingales with Lazy Lower Bounds
arxiv-2304-11363.creator: Toru Takisaka 1, Libo Zhang 2, Changjiang Wang 1, Jiamou Liu 2
arxiv-2304-11363.description: Abstract Lexicographic Ranking SuperMartingale (LexRSM) is a probabilistic extension of Lexicographic Ranking Function (LexRF), which is a widely accepted technique for verifying program termination. In this paper, we are the first to propose sound probabilistic extensions of LexRF with a weaker non-negativity condition, called single-component (SC) non-negativity.

arxiv-2306-06516.title: Various disguises of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator
arxiv-2306-06516.creator: Mahmut Elbistan, Krzysztof Andrzejewski
arxiv-2306-06516.description: Abstract Beginning with a simple set of planar equations, we discuss novel realizations of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator in various contexts. First, due to the bi-Hamiltonian character of this model, we develop a Hamiltonian approach for the Eisenhart-Duval lift of the related dynamics. We apply this approach to the previously worked example of a circularly polarized periodic gravitational wave.

arxiv-2405-13961.title: SADDLe: Sharpness-Aware Decentralized Deep Learning with Heterogeneous Data
arxiv-2405-13961.creator: Sakshi Choudhary, Sai Aparna Aketi, Kaushik Roy
arxiv-2405-13961.description: Abstract Decentralized training enables learning with distributed datasets generated at different locations without relying on a central server. In realistic scenarios, the data distribution across these sparsely connected learning agents can be significantly heterogeneous, leading to local model over-fitting and poor global model generalization.

arxiv-2408-05611.creator: William Chang, Colin Defant, Daniel Frishberg
arxiv-2408-05611.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by William Chang, Colin Defant, Daniel Frishberg. Eppstein and Frishberg recently proved that the mixing time for the simple random walk on the 1 1 -skeleton of the associahedron is O ⁡ ( n 3 ​ log 3 ​ n ) O(n^{3}\log^{3}n) . We obtain similar rapid mixing results for the simple random walks on the 1 1 -skeleta of the type- B B and type- D D associahedra.

arxiv-2505-18165.title: A Comprehensive PPG-based Dataset for HR/HRV Studies
arxiv-2505-18165.creator: Jingye Xu 1 , Yuntong Zhang 2 , Wei Wang 1 , Mimi Xie 1 , Dakai Zhu 1
arxiv-2505-18165.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jingye Xu 1 , Yuntong Zhang 2 , Wei Wang 1 , Mimi Xie 1 , Dakai Zhu 1. Heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) are important vital signs for human physical and mental health. Recent research has demonstrated that photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors can infer HR and HRV. However, it is difficult to find a comprehensive PPG-based dataset for HR/HRV studies, especially for various study needs: multiple scenes, long-term monitoring, and multimodality (multiple PPG channels and extra acceleration data).

arxiv-2509-05116.title: Analyzing Gait Adaptation with Hemiplegia Simulation Suits and Digital Twins
arxiv-2509-05116.creator: Jialin Chen, Jeremie Clos, Dominic Price, Praminda Caleb-Solly
arxiv-2509-05116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jialin Chen, Jeremie Clos, Dominic Price, Praminda Caleb-Solly. To advance the development of assistive and rehabilitation robots, it is essential to conduct experiments early in the design cycle. However, testing early prototypes directly with users can pose safety risks. To address this, we explore the use of condition-specific simulation suits worn by healthy participants in controlled environments as a means to study gait changes associated with various impairments and support rapid prototyping.

arxiv-2509-07684.title: Benchmarking the Plane-Wave Born and Distorted Waves approximations for electron-impact collision strength computations: the sample case of Sr II
arxiv-2509-07684.creator: Jérôme Deprincesup1,2, Lucas Maisonsup1
arxiv-2509-07684.description: Abstract The discovery of gravitational waves from a neutron star merger in 2017 (GW170817) and the associated kilonova (AT2017gfo) confirmed these events as key sites for heavy element production through the r-process. Subsequent observations, including late-time spectra with JWST , have highlighted the need for accurate modeling of kilonova ejecta.

pmc-11396152.creator: Roop Kaw, Kara Dupuy-McCauley, Jean Wong
pmc-11396152.description: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) can often be underdiagnosed or misdiagnosed and has been shown to pose significant risks in perioperative situations. Patients with OHS have a higher prevalence of baseline morbid conditions like hypertension, congestive heart failure (CHF), diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary hypertension (PH), which contribute to adverse postoperative outcomes.

Methods This Institutional Review Board-approved study consisted of a voluntary online survey of U.S. medical students.

pmc-13253154.title: Mitochondria-targeted cuproptosis-driven nanoplatform for synergistic photothermal/chemodynamic therapy and systemic antitumor immunotherapy
pmc-13253154.creator: Hui Zhang, Yuting Lu, Jingchun Wang, Yikai Ma, Yuanjin Sun, Shengzhong Rong, Xu Zhu, Yingxue Jin
pmc-13253154.description: Cuproptosis, a recently identified copper-dependent regulated cell death pathway driven by mitochondrial lipoylated protein aggregation, holds considerable promise for cancer therapy. Its clinical translation is constrained by off-target toxicity of free copper ions, inadequate mitochondria-targeted delivery and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. We developed a hyaluronic acid-camouflaged, pH-responsive nanoplatform HACCR for mitochondria-targeted, cuproptosis-driven synergistic therapy and systemic antitumor immunity.

pmc-13324753.title: Evaluation of bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortopathic changes using third-generation dual-source computed tomography
pmc-13324753.creator: Salai Thanihaivel E, Arun Sharma, Mansi Verma, Rajesh Vijayvergiya, Manphool Singhal
pmc-13324753.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) affects 0.5%-2% of the population and is associated with progressive aortopathy leading to life-threatening complications. Aortic size index (ASI) adjusts aortic dimensions for body surface area (BSA), potentially improving risk stratification.AIMTo characterise BAV-associated aortopathic changes using third-generation dual-source computed tomography (CT) and to derive a cohort-specific ASI threshold associated with CT-defined ascending aortic dilatation in an Indian population.METHODSThis prospective cross-sectional study enrolled 100 BAV patients (age > 18 years) from July 2022 to November 2023.
